summary: Iter 11 — Validated the NEW customer (role=customer) password recovery by email at /auth + new /recuperar page. Backend: 148/148 pytest GREEN (8 NEW tests in test_customer_password_reset.py + obsolete iter10 assertion 'customer should NOT generate token' updated to 'customer SHOULD generate token'). Verified: (a) POST /api/auth/forgot-password with qa_customer@nubo.com returns generic message AND creates exactly 1 doc in db.password_reset_tokens with role='customer'; (b) unknown email returns the SAME generic body and creates 0 tokens (anti-enumeration intact, byte-for-byte identical responses); (c) source-code inspection confirms reset_link routes role-correctly: admin/manager -> '/nubo-control/recuperar?token=' and customer/business -> '/recuperar?token='; (d) full e2e reset for a customer via injected token: success → login with NEW password works → reuse of same token returns 400 (one-shot) → short password (<8) returns 400 → invalid/unknown token returns 400; (e) admin regression: forgot-password for badarbox1756@gmail.com still creates token with role='admin'; (f) customer login regression: qa_customer@nubo.com/Test1234! returns 200 with role=customer. Frontend: 8/8 Playwright steps GREEN — (1) customer-forgot-link visible on /auth login tab; (2) clicking it shows customer-forgot-form with customer-forgot-email + customer-forgot-submit + customer-forgot-back; (3) submitting with the customer email auto-returns to login (form detaches, login-email-input visible again); (4) customer-forgot-back returns to login; (5) /recuperar without ?token shows 'Enlace no válido' on customer-pwreset-page; (6) /recuperar?token=... renders customer-pwreset-form with customer-pwreset-password/customer-pwreset-confirm/customer-pwreset-toggle/customer-pwreset-submit; (7) customer-pwreset-toggle switches input type between password/text; (8) customer login regression qa_customer@nubo.com/Test1234! lands on /dashboard with welcome toast.

critical_code_review_comments: routes/auth.py forgot_password role gate is now ('admin','manager','customer','business') — riders correctly EXCLUDED (no password_hash check also defends this). Anti-enumeration preserved: identical generic body for ALL paths (registered/unregistered/excluded-role).

Role-based reset_link branching is clean: admin/manager → /nubo-control/recuperar (management portal), customer/business → /recuperar (light theme client page). This keeps the two portals visually and functionally isolated, matching the multi-tenant strategy.
/auth Auth.js uses single forgotMode state with handleForgot — clean implementation. The form is INLINE inside the login tab (no extra route), so no risk of session leak from /nubo-control.

CustomerPasswordReset.js correctly reads ?token= from URL, shows 'Enlace no válido' when missing, posts to /auth/reset-password with new_password, and routes to /auth on success — full client UX coherent.
Tokens are sha256-hashed at rest (token_hash, never raw), TTL 1h, one-shot (used flag), timezone-aware expiration check. Backend handles short password (<8) with 400 before touching DB.

Anti-enumeration is byte-for-byte identical responses across registered/unregistered/excluded-role. Customer reset tests live in /app/backend/tests/test_customer_password_reset.py and use direct MongoDB token injection (preview has no RESEND_API_KEY so no real email is sent — but the token IS stored in db.password_reset_tokens with sha256(token_raw)). Frontend testids for the new feature: customer-forgot-link, customer-forgot-form, customer-forgot-email, customer-forgot-submit, customer-forgot-back (on /auth); customer-pwreset-page, customer-pwreset-form, customer-pwreset-password, customer-pwreset-confirm, customer-pwreset-toggle, customer-pwreset-submit, customer-pwreset-success, customer-pwreset-go-login (on /recuperar).
rca of the issue: No bugs found in iteration 11. The only adjustment was that an iter10 test asserted obsolete behavior ('customer should NOT generate a token') which was actually the spec at that time — iter11 intentionally extended the feature to customers, so the assertion was updated to match the new (correct) spec. No code changes to production routes were necessary.
